title: Tricks for 8s and 9s
goal: I can use my 4s to find 8s, and my 10s to find 9s.

card.desc: Bristol learns two shortcuts. ×8 = double the 4s (8 × 6: 4 × 6 = 24, double it to 48). ×9 = ×10 minus one group (9 × 7: 70 − 7 = 63). Both tricks start from facts she already knows, so she stops counting one by one.

win: You know two big tricks now. 8s and 9s, here you come!

slides.title: Tricks for 8s and 9s
slides.text: You learned two tricks in class. Now use them on your own. 💪 At the end, show what you know!

slides.title: Say the tricks
slides.text: Say each one out loud. Tell a grown-up if one is near.
prompts: How do you find 8 × a number?
How do you find 9 × a number?
What is the problem in your book?

slides.title: Two tricks
slides.text: Both tricks start with facts you know.
slides.tip: Type your answer. You get 3 tries.

items.q: To find 8 × 8, what do you double?
items.why: 8 groups is two sets of 4 groups. Double 32 is 64.
no: 8 + 8 is only 2 groups of 8. Start with the 4s.
10 × 8 is the start for the 9s trick.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Take away one group of 8. So 9 × 8 = ____
Which way finds 9 × 6?
no: Each group is 6. Take away 6, not 9.
That is the 8s trick. It makes 8 × 6.

slides.title: Which fact does it help?
slides.text: Each card is a step. Does it help find 8 × 7 or 9 × 7?

items.hint: Is this a 4s fact or a 10s fact?
Is this doubling or taking away?

items.why: One group less than 10 groups is 9 × 7.
items.hint: Is this doubling or taking away?

items.why: 8 groups is two sets of 4 groups.
9 groups is one group less than 10.

slides.title: How to do 9 × 8
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.

items.q: Liz says 9 × 6 = 59. That is wrong. Type the right answer: 9 × 6 = ____
items.no: Liz took away 1. Take away a whole group of 6.

items.q: Marion says 8 × 7 = 32. That is wrong. Type the right answer: 8 × 7 = ____
items.no: Marion added 4. Double the 4s fact instead.

items.q: Amy has 9 bags. Each bag has 7 bones. How many bones?
Ellie has 8 stickers. Liz has 5 stickers. How many stickers in all?
items.why: 8 and 5 are not equal groups. Add: 8 + 5 = 13.
items.no: These are two different amounts. Do not multiply.

items.q: There are 9 kids. Each kid has 2 socks. Do you multiply or add? Type multiply or add.
items.no: Is every group the same size?
items.hint: Each kid has 2. Same size groups.

sets.q: Which is the 8s trick for 8 × 7?
sets.why: 8 is double 4. So find 4 × 7, then double it.
no: That is the 9s trick. It makes 9 × 7 = 63.
Double, do not add 4.

sets.q: Which is the 9s trick for 9 × 7?
sets.why: Start with 10 × 7 = 70. Take away one group of 7.
no: Each group is 7, so take away 7.
Take away a whole group of 7, not 1.

sets.q: A vet has 8 dogs. Each dog gets 9 treats. How many treats?
Ellie plants 9 rows of seeds. Each row has 6 seeds. How many seeds?
Marion has 9 stamps. Amy gives her 8 more. How many stamps now?
sets.why: 9 and 8 are not equal groups. Add: 9 + 8 = 17.
no: These are not equal groups. Add.
1 is 9 − 8. She got more stamps.

sets.q: What is 8 × 6?
no: 42 is 7 × 6. Find 4 × 6 and double it.
54 is 9 × 6. This is 8 groups of 6.

sets.q: Which is the 8s trick for 8 × 9?
no: That is the 9s trick. It makes 9 × 9.
Double the 36. Do not add 8.

sets.q: Liz finds 9 × 8 like this: 80 − 9. What is wrong?
choices: She should add 8, not take away.
no: Adding makes 11 groups. We need one group less.

sets.q: Amy's mom sees 9 dogs every day. How many dogs does she see in 5 days?
sets.no: She sees 9 dogs each day for 5 days. Multiply.

sets.q: There are 8 cats. Each cat has 4 legs. How many legs?
Marion has 8 pens. Liz has 9 pens. How many pens in all?
no: 8 and 9 are not equal groups. Add.
1 is 9 − 8. The question asks how many in all.

sets.q: There are 8 rows of stars. Each row has 7 stars. How many stars?
no: 49 is 7 × 7. There are 8 rows.
Close! Double 28: 40 + 16 = 56.

sets.q: Which is the 9s trick for 9 × 4?
no: Take away a whole group of 4, not 1.
That is the 8s trick. It makes 8 × 4.

sets.q: Ellie finds 8 × 6 like this: 4 × 6 = 24, then 24 + 4. What is wrong?
no: Taking away is the 9s trick.

sets.q: There are 8 kids. Each kid gets 7 stickers. How many stickers?
Amy has 9 bones. She finds 9 more. How many bones now?
no: That is 9 groups of 9. Here there are just two amounts.
She found more. The number goes up.

sets.q: What is 9 × 5?
no: 49 is 50 − 1. Take away a whole group of 5.
54 is 9 × 6. This is 9 groups of 5.

practice.intro: You get 3 tries on each one. Only your first try counts. 8s: double the 4s. 9s: 10s take away one group.

no: 100 is 10 × 10. Take away one group of 10.
Double, do not add 4.
That is the 9s trick. 90 − 9 = 81, which is 9 × 9.

questions.q: A vet has 9 cages. Each cage has 2 kittens. How many kittens?
no: 11 is 9 + 2. Each cage has 2, so multiply.
16 is 8 × 2. Count the cages: 9.

questions.q: Amy reads 8 pages a day for 5 days. How many pages?
questions.hint: Count by 5s eight times, or double 4 × 5.

questions.q: Liz has 9 beads. Ellie has 6 beads. How many in all?

pages.title: Part 1: Double the 4s
pages.directions: Find the 4s fact. Then double it to get the 8s fact.

pages.title: Part 2: 10s take away one group
pages.directions: Find the 10s fact. Take away one group to get the 9s fact.

pages.title: Part 3: Draw it
pages.directions: Draw an array. Then write the answer.

items.text: 9. Draw 8 rows of 2 dots. Circle the top 4 rows. That is 4 × 2. Double it. 8 × 2 = _____
10. There are 8 dog beds. Each bed has 4 puppies. How many puppies?
11. Marion has 9 bows. Ellie has 7 bows. How many bows in all?
12. Amy fills 9 bags. Each bag has 5 dog biscuits. How many biscuits?

pages.title: Part 5: Book corner
pages.directions: Write about Amy and the Missing Puppy. Use a capital letter and a period.

items.text: 13. What is the problem in the story so far?

teacher.objective: Bristol finds 8s facts by doubling the 4s fact (8 × 6: 4 × 6 = 24, double to 48) and 9s facts by taking one group away from the 10s fact (9 × 7: 70 − 7 = 63). Both tricks build on facts she owns, so she stops skip-counting from zero.
materials: Zoom with screen share (open the Class lesson and type the teacher code); your whiteboard on camera
At home: about 40 beans or counters, paper and pencil
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Packet (2 pages): you send it home after Tuesday's lesson, with the Lesson 7 packet

plan.do: Class slide 1. Check she has beans, paper, pencil and her book on camera. She names the facts she knows fast.
Class slide 2. Main character, problem, what she tried. Push for a full sentence with because.
Class slide 3. She says the trick out loud before each answer; you tap what she says.

Class slides 4–8. Bean rows on camera: 4 rows of 3, then 4 more rows. Quick check (slide 5): she says, you type. Whiteboard: double 24 with tens then ones (slide 6), then she doubles 16, 28 and 36 (slide 7) and taps the 8s facts (slide 8).
Class slides 9–11. She builds 10 rows of 4 and pushes one row away. Ask: 1 or 4? Then 9 × 7 on the whiteboard and three taps.
Class slides 12–14. Which trick? (she says double or take away before she answers), build 9 pots of 3, then the call-out: she says the trick and the answer before you click.
Class slide 15. She reads aloud and says equal groups or not before she answers.
Class slide 16. She says both tricks. Show the task list: tonight only the after-class lesson (with Show What You Know) and 10 minutes of reading.

watch: For 9s, taking away 9 or 1 instead of one group (9 × 6 = 51 or 59). Ask: what is in one group?
For 8s, adding 4 instead of doubling (8 × 7 = 32). Ask: how many groups of 7 did we have? How many do we need?
Doubling 2-digit numbers: 28 + 28 = 46 (forgot to regroup). Have her double tens, then ones, then add.
Saying 7 × 8 = 54. Fix it now: 4 × 7 = 28, double is 56.

packet_key.answer: 8 rows of 2 dots with 4 rows circled; 8 × 2 = 16
A complete sentence naming the problem (for example, a puppy is missing), with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Tomorrow (Lesson 7) is in person, so bring beans and cups. Her Show What You Know comes from tonight's after-class lesson (she needs 85, 7 of 8; a retake gets a new set). If she scores under 85, start Lesson 7 with 5 minutes of bean rows: 4 rows doubled, then 10 rows minus one row, before the 7s. This lesson's practice and packet are on Tuesday's task list.

tasks: Monday night: do the After-class lesson. Finish Show What You Know (get 85).
Monday night: read your book for 10 minutes. Find the problem in the story.

slides.title: Tricks for 8s and 9s
slides.text: 8s and 9s look big. But you already know the secret. 🤫 Today you use 4s and 10s to find them.

notes.do: Before you start: she has about 40 beans (or counters), paper, a pencil and her book next to her, on camera. Share your screen. Today is Zoom, so she says every answer and you tap or type exactly what she says.
notes.say: Today we learn two tricks for the biggest facts: 8s and 9s. You already know the facts that make them work.
notes.ask: Which facts do you know really fast?
notes.listen: 2s, 5s, 10s, and last week's 4s and 6s. If she leaves out 4s and 6s, remind her: last week you learned double-double for 4s and 5s-plus-one-group for 6s.

slides.title: Who has a problem?
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: Who is the main character? How do you know?
What did she do to try to fix it?

notes.do: Book open on camera. Give her time to look back at a page.
notes.say: Book first. Tell me about the main character and her problem.
notes.ask: Who is the main character? What is her problem? Why is it a problem for her?
notes.listen: A full sentence that names Amy and tells the problem in her own words, with because. If she says only one word ("the puppy"), ask her to say the whole sentence with a starter.

slides.title: 4s and 6s warm-up
slides.text: These are from last week. Use your tricks!

items.q: Each puppy has 4 paws. How many paws on 7 puppies?
items.why: 7 × 4 is the same as 4 × 7. Double 7 is 14. Double 14 is 28.
no: 21 is 7 × 3. Each puppy has 4 paws.
24 is 6 × 4. Count the puppies: 7.

items.q: What is 6 × 8?
no: You added 6. Add one more group of 8.
54 is 6 × 9. This is 6 groups of 8.

items.q: Amy has 6 bags. Each bag has 9 treats. How many treats?
items.why: Equal groups, so multiply. 5 × 9 = 45. One more group of 9: 45 + 9 = 54.
no: 15 is 6 + 9. Every bag has 9, so multiply.
You added 6. Add one more group of 9.

notes.say: Before you answer, tell me the trick. 4s: double, double. 6s: 5s plus one more group.
notes.ask: For 7 puppies with 4 paws: what is double 7? What is double that?
notes.listen: "Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28." If she counts by 4s on her fingers, stop her and ask for the double-double. For 6 × 8: "5 × 8 is 40, plus one more 8 is 48."

slides.title: 8 is double 4
slides.text: To find 8 × a number, find 4 × first. Then double it.

steps.text: Step 2. Make another 4 rows. Now there are 8 rows.

visual.label: 4 rows of 3 and 4 more rows of 3

slides.tip: 8 groups is just two sets of 4 groups.

notes.do: On camera she makes 4 rows of 3 beans. Then 4 more rows right under them. Click next step as she builds.
notes.say: Look. 4 rows, then 4 more rows. That is 8 rows. 8 groups is two sets of 4 groups.
notes.ask: The top part is 4 × 3. What is it? The bottom part is the same. So what is the total?
notes.listen: "12 and 12 is 24." Wrong: 16 (she added 4 beans, not 4 more rows of 3). Point to the bottom 4 rows and count them with her.

items.q: 4 rows and 4 more rows make ____ rows.
items.why: 4 + 4 = 8. 8 rows is two sets of 4 rows.

notes.do: She says each answer. You type exactly what she says. If she is wrong, let the page say try again.
notes.ask: How many rows now? Then: what is double 20?
notes.listen: 8 rows. 40. If she says 24 for 8 × 5, she added 4. Ask: did we add 4 beans, or 4 whole rows?

slides.title: Double a bigger number
slides.tip: Doubling is adding a number to itself. Tens first, then ones.

notes.do: Whiteboard on camera. Write 24 + 24 in a tens column and a ones column.
notes.say: Doubling a big number is easy if we go in two parts. Double the tens. Then double the ones. Then put them together.
notes.ask: What is double 20? Double 4? Now put 40 and 8 together.
notes.listen: "40 and 8 is 48." Wrong: 44 or 28 (she doubled only one part). Point to the part she skipped.

slides.title: Double tens, then ones
slides.text: Double the tens. Double the ones. Put them together.

items.q: Double 16. Tens: 10 + 10 = 20. Ones: 6 + 6 = 12. Together: ____
Double 28. Tens: 20 + 20 = 40. Ones: 8 + 8 = 16. Together: ____
items.no: Add 40 and 16. 16 has a ten in it!

items.q: Double 36 = ____
items.no: Double the tens. Double the ones. Then add.

notes.do: She works each one on paper first, then tells you the answer to type.
notes.say: Tens first. Then ones. Then put them together.
notes.listen: 56 for double 28. Watch for 46: she forgot the extra ten in 8 + 8 = 16. Ask: how many tens are in 16?

no: Not 54. Double 28: tens first, then ones.
35 is 28 + 7. Double means add 28 again.

items.q: What is 8 × 4?
no: 16 is 4 × 4. You need to double it one more time.
24 is 8 × 3. This is 8 groups of 4.

items.q: There are 8 boxes. Each box has 8 crayons. How many crayons?
no: 16 is 8 + 8. That is only 2 boxes. There are 8 boxes.
56 is 7 × 8. Count the boxes again: 8.

notes.say: Now use it. Find the 4s fact. Then double it.
notes.ask: Before you answer: what is the 4s fact? What is double that?
notes.listen: "4 × 7 is 28. Double 28 is 56." If she picks 54, it is the old 7 × 8 = 54 mistake: make her double 28 out loud, tens then ones.

slides.title: 9 is 10 take away 1 group
slides.text: 10s are easy. So find 10 × first. Then take away one group.

steps.text: Step 2. Take away one row of 4. Now there are 9 rows.

slides.tip: Take away one group, not 9 and not 1.

notes.do: On camera she makes 10 rows of 4 beans. Then she pushes one row away.
notes.say: 10s are the easiest facts. 9 groups is just one group less than 10 groups.
notes.ask: How many beans did you push away: 1 or 4? Why 4?
notes.listen: "4, because one row has 4." If she says 1, point at the row: count the beans in it.

slides.title: Try 9 × 7
slides.tip: The group is the number you multiply by. For 9 × 7, the group is 7.

notes.say: For 9 × 7, the group is 7. So we take away 7.
notes.ask: Which number is in each group? So what do we take away?
notes.listen: "7." Wrong: 9 (she takes away the 9) or 1 (she takes away one bean). Ask: how many are in one group?

no: 51 is 60 − 9. Take away a group of 6, not 9.
59 is 60 − 1. Take away a whole group of 6.

items.q: What is 9 × 8?
no: 71 is 80 − 9. Take away one group of 8.
64 is 8 × 8. Start with 10 × 8 = 80.

items.q: Which way finds 9 × 5?
no: Take away one group. Each group is 5, not 9.
Adding makes 11 groups. We need one group less.

notes.say: Say the 10s fact first. Then say what you take away.
notes.ask: For 9 × 8: what is 10 × 8? What is in one group?
notes.listen: "80, take away 8, 72." If she picks 71, she took away 9. Go back to the bean rows.

items.q: This step: 24 + 24 = 48. Which fact does it find?
no: 9s take away from the 10s. This step doubles.
4 × 6 is only 24. Doubling makes 8 groups.

items.q: This step: 60 − 6 = 54. Which fact does it find?
items.why: 60 is 10 × 6. Take away one group of 6: 9 × 6 = 54.
no: 8s double the 4s. This step takes away.
6 × 6 is 36. This step starts at 60.

items.q: To find 9 × 8, what do you find first?
no: 4 × 8 is the first step for 8 × 8.
Keep the 8. 10 groups of 8 is 10 × 8.

notes.say: Each one is a step. Tell me: is it a double step or a take away step? Then tell me your answer.
notes.ask: Which trick starts with the 4s? Which trick starts with the 10s?
notes.listen: Doubling goes with 8s. Taking away from the 10s goes with 9s. If she picks 4 × 6 for the first one, ask: how many groups after we double?

slides.title: Ellie's flower pots
slides.text: Ellie has 9 pots. Each pot has 3 flowers. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each pot is one group. Set Groups to the number of pots. Set In each group to the flowers in one pot.

notes.do: She also makes 9 piles of 3 beans on camera. She tells you the groups and how many in each; you click the + buttons.
notes.ask: How many pots? How many in each pot? Which trick finds 9 × 3?

slides.title: Say the trick, then the answer
slides.text: I say a fact. You say the trick. Then you say the answer. Then we check.

steps.text: Listen for the fact. Say the trick and the answer first. Then we check here.

notes.do: Say each fact out loud (8 × 10, 9 × 2, 8 × 9, 9 × 5). She says the trick and the answer first. Then click next step to check it.
notes.say: I say the fact. You tell me the trick and the answer.
notes.ask: Which trick? What is the first fact you find?
notes.listen: The trick word first (double, or take away), then the answer. If she just guesses the answer, ask her to show the trick.

items.q: There are 9 rows of chairs. Each row has 9 chairs. How many chairs?
no: 18 is 9 + 9. That is only 2 rows. There are 9 rows.
89 is 90 − 1. Take away one group of 9.

items.q: Liz has 8 shells. Marion has 6 shells. How many shells in all?
items.why: 8 and 6 are not equal groups. Add: 8 + 6 = 14.
no: 8 and 6 are two different groups. Don't multiply. Add.
2 is 8 − 6. The question asks how many in all.

items.q: The vet has 8 bunnies. Each bunny eats 3 carrots. How many carrots?
items.why: Equal groups, so multiply. 4 × 3 = 12. Double 12 is 24.
no: 11 is 8 + 3. Each bunny eats 3, so multiply.
21 is 7 × 3. Count the bunnies: 8.

notes.say: Before you answer, tell me: equal groups or not?
notes.ask: Is every group the same size? Which word tells you?
notes.listen: "Each row has 9" means equal groups: multiply. "8 shells and 6 shells" are two different amounts: add.

slides.title: Our two tricks
slides.text:
8s: find the 4s. Then double.
9s: find the 10s. Then take away one group.

steps.text: Tonight: do the After-class lesson. It ends with Show What You Know.
Then read your book for 10 minutes.

slides.tip: Tonight is short. The practice and the packet come tomorrow.

notes.say: Great work. Tonight is short: the after-class lesson and 10 minutes of reading. That's it.
notes.ask: Tell me the 8s trick. Tell me the 9s trick.
notes.listen: "Double the 4s." "10s take away one group." If she mixes them up, say both again with 8 × 7 and 9 × 7.
notes.do: Show the task list on the course page. Tell her tomorrow's lesson is in person.
